item.title: HAVING Clause in PostgreSQL: Filtering Aggregated Data
item.description: The HAVING clause in PostgreSQL is a powerful tool for filtering aggregated data in the result set of a query. This clause enables developers to specify conditions for grouped results, allowing for more complex and targeted analysis. This article explores how to use the HAVING clause effectively in PostgreSQL. 1. Basic Syntax: The basic syntax of the HAVING clause is similar to the WHERE clause but is used specifically for conditions on aggregated data.

item.title: Numeric in PostgreSQL
item.description: How To Use NUMERIC in PostgreSQL PostgreSQL provides the NUMERIC data type for storing numeric values with high precision. This article will guide you through the usage of the NUMERIC type for accurate numeric calculations. Practical Example -- Example: Using NUMERIC for precise calculations SELECT CAST('123.456' AS NUMERIC) * 2 AS result; In this example, we cast a string to the NUMERIC type and perform a multiplication operation. FAQs on Using NUMERIC in PostgreSQL Q: What is the advantage of using NUMERIC over other numeric types?

item.title: Using INTERVAL in PostgreSQL
item.description: How To Use INTERVAL in PostgreSQL The INTERVAL data type in PostgreSQL allows you to store and manipulate periods of time. In this article, we’ll explore how to use INTERVAL in PostgreSQL for various time-related operations. Practical Example -- Example: Calculating the difference between two timestamps SELECT TIMESTAMP '2024-01-21 12:00:00' - TIMESTAMP '2024-01-20 10:30:00' AS time_difference; In this example, we subtract one timestamp from another to get the time difference.

item.title: What is Trigger in SQL? 2023
item.description: Trigger is a special type of stored procedure that is executed automatically in response to certain events on a database table Triggers are used to enforce business rules, maintain data integrity, and perform tasks such as auditing. Triggers can be activated by various events, such as INSERT , UPDATE , DELETE , or SELECT statements on a table, or by direct invocation using the EXECUTE or CALL statement. Triggers can also be activated by database events such as logon, logoff, or server startup.
